summary.stop_text: Quality stop (QA hold): reject rate high on consecutive checks

steps: Check ST60-VIS telemetry for reject_rate_pct and cycle_time_s across the history window; an abrupt jump versus a gradual trend will determine whether the QA hold was triggered by a sudden failure or progressive degradation.

Inspect ST40-SLR bead_width_mm, flow_rate_ccm, and pump_pressure_bar; deviations outside nominal ranges (e.g., bead width outside 3.6-4.4 mm or pressure outside 105-135 bar) would support sealer application defect as the cause of visual rejects, whereas nominal readings refute sealer failure.

Examine ST30-WLD and ST20-WLD weld_current_ka and tip_resistance_mohm; readings outside normal limits (weld current outside 9.8-11.2 kA or tip resistance >0.175 mOhm) would support weld quality defects triggering downstream visual inspection failure, while nominal readings refute weld defect causes.

Check ST50-CNV speed_mpm and vibration_rms_mms leading up to the stop; elevated vibration (>2.8 mm/s) or speed instability outside 11.5-12.5 m/min would support part mispositioning or camera motion blur during inspection, whereas nominal readings refute conveyor drive instability.

Review UT-AIR header_pressure_bar; supply pressure dropping below 6.0 bar would support pneumatic actuator or clamp starvation affecting upstream tooling consistency, whereas pressure maintained within 6.0-7.5 bar refutes utility air failure.

Evaluate whether ST60-VIS reject spike is a sensor or data problem (such as lens contamination, illumination drift, or vision algorithm false-positives) by verifying if reject rates spiked despite all upstream process parameters (bead width, weld parameters) remaining well within nominal tolerances.

citations.quote: A narrow bead with normal flow and pressure points to the nozzle or the bead program; a narrow bead with low flow points to the pump supply (see Section 6.2).

Outlet pressure (`pump_pressure_bar`) starts to pulse at the pump stroke rate (0.15 Hz, one stroke about every 6.7 s) and its mean falls. Flow (`flow_rate_ccm`) drops below its normal range of 270 to 330 cc/min. Motor current falls slightly and becomes unsteady because the pump moves less material.
The bead becomes narrow and uneven (A-ST40-BEAD-QA) and ST60 rejects rise. The pump sounds rough, with a knock on each stroke.

repair_steps: Inspect the pump inlet line and material supply feed for cavitation, air ingress, or drum supply issues.
Remove and inspect the inlet strainer basket for debris, clogging, or material buildup.
Clean or replace the inlet strainer basket.
Inspect follower plate and drum seal seating on the material drum.

steps.text: Identify every energy source for the sealer from Table 8-1 and collect one personal lock and tag for each isolating device.

citation.quote: Identify every energy source for the sealer from Table 8-1 and collect one personal lock and tag for each isolating device.

steps.text: Notify the line lead and the ST40 operator that the sealer pump will be shut down and locked out.

citation.quote: Notify the line lead and the ST40 operator that the sealer pump will be shut down and locked out.

steps.text: Finish the current bead, then stop the pump with the pump stop push-button on the sealer panel.

citation.quote: Finish the current bead, then stop the pump with the pump stop push-button on the sealer panel.

steps.text: Lower the follower plate onto the drum or rest the ram on its mechanical stop before the ram air is shut off.

citation.quote: Lower the follower plate onto the drum or rest the ram on its mechanical stop before the ram air is shut off.

steps.text: Switch the sealer pump main disconnect switch to OFF.

citation.quote: Switch the sealer pump main disconnect switch to OFF.

steps.text: Close the ram air lockout valve so that its exhaust port vents the ram and nozzle air circuit.

citation.quote: Close the ram air lockout valve so that its exhaust port vents the ram and nozzle air circuit.

steps.text: Fit a personal lock and tag to the sealer pump main disconnect switch and to the ram air lockout valve.

citation.quote: Fit a personal lock and tag to the sealer pump main disconnect switch and to the ram air lockout valve.

steps.text: Point the nozzle into a waste container and open the material relief valve until the material pressure gauge reads zero.

citation.quote: Point the nozzle into a waste container and open the material relief valve until the material pressure gauge reads zero.

steps.text: Keep every material hose and fitting closed until the material pressure gauge reads zero.

citation.quote: Keep every material hose and fitting closed until the material pressure gauge reads zero.

steps.text: Check the material pressure gauge again before each new task and reopen the relief valve if it reads above zero.

citation.quote: Check the material pressure gauge again before each new task and reopen the relief valve if it reads above zero.

steps.text: Press the pump start push-button and the nozzle purge button to confirm that nothing starts, moves or dispenses, then return both controls to off.

citation.quote: Press the pump start push-button and the nozzle purge button to confirm that nothing starts, moves or dispenses, then return both controls to off.

steps.text: Test for absence of voltage at the pump motor terminals with a tester proven on a known live source before and after the test.

citation.quote: Test for absence of voltage at the pump motor terminals with a tester proven on a known live source before and after the test.

Remove tools, waste containers and nonessential items, and confirm that every hose, fitting and the nozzle are tight and intact.

steps.text: Close the material relief valve.

steps.text: Check that all employees are clear of the pump, the drum ram and the dispense area.
